risks.summary: Authenticated user email is propagated into public GitHub workflow inputs and historical public evidence.
risks.impact: Personal identifiers and tenant identity can be disclosed through a public repository execution plane.
risks.acceptance: No full email address appears in workflow inputs, logs, artifacts, PR comments, or public audit evidence.

risks.summary: Application authentication has no user allowlist, account status, plan, quota, record limit, symbol limit, or job limit.
risks.impact: A publicly usable OAuth configuration could create uncontrolled D1, GitHub Actions, and market-data load.
risks.acceptance: Tenant status and quotas are enforced server-side with owner access preserved during rollout.

risks.summary: Preview Pages deployments can resolve to the production Worker and production D1 because of frontend fallback and permissive preview CORS.
risks.impact: Pull-request previews can read or mutate production tenant data.
risks.acceptance: Preview builds use a staging Worker, staging D1, and staging OAuth client; production rejects preview origins.

risks.summary: The portfolio model has no cash ledger, deposits, withdrawals, settlement, liabilities, receivables, or account structure.
risks.impact: Displayed total value cannot represent a brokerage account NAV and becomes zero after full liquidation despite remaining cash.
risks.acceptance: Account NAV reconciles securities, cash, receivables, unsettled items, and liabilities to broker-statement fixtures.

risks.summary: Current TWR and XIRR describe security-project cash flows rather than a complete brokerage account, while UI terminology implies account-level performance.
risks.impact: Users can make decisions from materially misleading performance labels.
risks.acceptance: Legacy metrics are explicitly named and Account TWR/MWRR is shown only after cash-ledger reconciliation.

risks.summary: A transaction tagged to multiple groups is fully copied into every group, duplicating quantities, fees, taxes, dividends, and sells.
risks.impact: Group results can oversell and cannot add back to the all-portfolio result.
risks.acceptance: Strategy allocations satisfy quantity, fee, and tax conservation invariants or are explicitly labeled as non-additive overlapping analysis.

risks.summary: GroupManager can send forbidden owner fields, does not consistently check response.ok, and reports sequential partial updates as success.
risks.impact: Users can receive false success while records are unchanged or only partially changed.
risks.acceptance: Every mutation checks HTTP and application status; partial failure is visible and atomic batch APIs are used before accounting cutover.

risks.summary: The browser reads only the first records page while the Python runner follows all cursor pages.
risks.impact: After 1,000 records, the UI and group tools silently operate on a truncated ledger while calculations use the full ledger.
risks.acceptance: UI record count, API record count, and runner record count are identical for fixtures above 1,000 and 10,000 records.

risks.summary: Full transaction records are written to localStorage without a meaningful offline read path.
risks.impact: XSS, shared-device, and stale-data exposure increases without providing a reliable offline feature.
risks.acceptance: Transaction payloads are not persisted in localStorage and legacy cached_records is removed on startup.

risks.summary: Record creates and updates lack client mutation identity, record revision, optimistic locking, and external broker deduplication keys.
risks.impact: Retries can duplicate trades and multi-tab edits can silently overwrite newer data.
risks.acceptance: Duplicate requests are idempotent and stale revisions fail with a deterministic conflict response.

risks.summary: Snapshots do not bind to input ledger revision, job identity, methodology version, benchmark identity, market-data version, or source timestamps.
risks.impact: An older calculation can complete later and become the latest visible result.
risks.acceptance: Only a snapshot matching the current expected input revision can atomically become latest; stale results are superseded.

risks.summary: Estimated dividends are included in realized P&L and XIRR before payment, while confirmed entries lose gross, withholding, and net structure.
risks.impact: Performance can include unpaid or duplicated income and cannot reconcile broker withholding.
risks.acceptance: Dividend entitlement, receivable, payment, gross, withholding, net, currency, and source event are separately represented and deduplicated.

risks.summary: yfinance is the single market-data dependency for a product described as SaaS or real-time.
risks.impact: Availability, licensing, rate limiting, schema drift, and source-quality failures can block every tenant calculation.
risks.acceptance: Market data has documented licensing, provider provenance, quality status, retry policy, and an independently verified fallback or reconciliation source.

risks.summary: A live quote overwrites the last historical daily bar even when the current trading day has no daily row.
risks.impact: Yesterday's close and historical Daily P&L or benchmark history can be contaminated by today's intraday quote.
risks.acceptance: Immutable EOD bars and live quotes are stored separately and history never changes when a live quote arrives.

risks.summary: FX, prices, splits, and unsupported-currency failures silently degrade to 32, 0, 1, or multiplier 1.
risks.impact: Internally reconciled snapshots can still be economically false because all paths share the same fallback assumptions.
risks.acceptance: Silent fallbacks are removed from publishable snapshots; degraded data is explicit and cannot be published as verified.

risks.summary: Documentation claims broad international support while unsupported currencies, including KRW, can default to USD or multiplier 1.
risks.impact: Foreign securities can be misvalued by an entire currency conversion factor.
risks.acceptance: Only explicitly supported currencies can publish verified valuations; unsupported instruments fail closed with a clear message.

risks.summary: Frontend, DailyPnLHelper, and MarketStageDetector implement inconsistent market-hours logic without official holiday or early-close calendars.
risks.impact: Refresh and Daily P&L as-of decisions can be wrong around DST, Taiwan Saturday morning, holidays, and early closes.
risks.acceptance: All scheduling and as-of decisions use one exchange-calendar service based on UTC instants.

risks.summary: Portfolio history dates are derived from held-asset calendars rather than an independent benchmark total-return calendar.
risks.impact: Benchmark-only trading or dividend days can be omitted, biasing relative performance.
risks.acceptance: Benchmark history uses its own calendar and an explicit join and coverage policy.

risks.summary: Canonical reconciliation shares the main engine's market source and economic assumptions.
risks.impact: Internal equality proves algebraic consistency but not external economic truth.
risks.acceptance: Broker-statement golden cases and independent market-data samples supplement algebra and ledger reconciliation.

risks.summary: Browser persistence and server idempotency expire after 15 minutes while workflow polling and execution can last 20 minutes or queue longer.
risks.impact: An active job can lose deduplication protection and be triggered again.
risks.acceptance: Idempotency remains until terminal state plus a retry window and active leases prevent duplicate work.

risks.summary: Interactive refresh uses a globally serialized GitHub Actions workflow that checks out and recalculates full history.
risks.impact: Three-minute refresh cannot scale and queue delay conflicts with browser and idempotency timeouts.
risks.acceptance: Tenant-scoped durable compute coalesces equivalent work and GitHub Actions remains only a tested fallback before cutover.

risks.summary: UTC date serialization can prefill the previous calendar day during Taiwan early morning hours.
risks.impact: Users can save a transaction under the wrong trade date.
risks.acceptance: Local trade date is generated without UTC conversion and covered across timezone boundary tests.

risks.summary: UI labels, currency symbols, sell totals, precision, readiness state, and chart assumptions can misrepresent backend data.
risks.impact: Correct backend values can still be presented with the wrong meaning or stale status.
risks.acceptance: Component and browser tests verify labels, formulas, currencies, empty states, stale states, and precision.

risks.summary: PWA claims, composables, manifest, and service worker are not coherently wired, while an old service worker may still control prior clients.
risks.impact: Existing clients can receive stale bundles or misleading offline behavior across incompatible deployments.
risks.acceptance: A tombstone unregisters legacy workers before either removing PWA claims or deploying a versioned tested Workbox implementation.

risks.summary: Google ID token and identity fields are stored in localStorage and multiple modules initialize Google Identity Services independently.
risks.impact: XSS can steal credentials and competing GIS callbacks can break refresh behavior.
risks.acceptance: A revocable HttpOnly SameSite session is primary, one GIS service owns initialization, and legacy bearer support is retired only after two compatible releases.

risks.summary: Email address is the persistent tenant key throughout records, snapshots, settings, jobs, and browser recovery.
risks.impact: Email changes can split or orphan tenant data and spread personal identifiers through infrastructure.
risks.acceptance: An internal tenant UUID keyed by Google subject owns data while email remains mutable profile metadata during transition.

risks.summary: Financial quantities and amounts use SQLite REAL, Python float, and JavaScript Number as authoritative values.
risks.impact: Rounding drift can accumulate across fractional shares, fees, FX, allocations, and long histories.
risks.acceptance: Fixed-point or Decimal fields dual-write with conservation and round-trip tests before becoming authoritative.

risks.summary: One JSON snapshot repeats complete history, holdings, day ledgers, lot ledgers, and anomalies per group under a one-megabyte request limit.
risks.impact: Large portfolios or many groups can exceed upload limits and duplicate storage.
risks.acceptance: Snapshot metadata and normalized or object-stored payloads remain bounded with explicit size and retention tests.

risks.summary: README and historical deployment documents overclaim SaaS, Korea, PWA, real-time, and other capabilities or describe obsolete deployment paths.
risks.impact: Operators can deploy obsolete code and users can rely on unsupported functionality.
risks.acceptance: Current capability, limitations, canonical deployment path, and archived historical files are clearly separated and versioned.

risks.summary: The repository lacks a matching LICENSE file, privacy policy, terms, SECURITY policy, data retention policy, and security contact.
risks.impact: Distribution rights, user expectations, disclosure handling, and personal-data obligations are undefined.
risks.acceptance: Legal and security documents match actual product behavior and are reviewed before public expansion.

risks.summary: CI builds the frontend but lacks frontend behavior tests, linting, TypeScript, accessibility, dependency scanning, SBOM, provenance, and immutable action pins.
risks.impact: Known frontend defects and compromised or drifting dependencies can pass a green build.
risks.acceptance: CI covers component, browser, accessibility, security, dependency, provenance, and exact-action-SHA gates.

risks.summary: Production deployment evidence is distributed across one-time workflows, PR comments, release notes, and endpoint responses.
risks.impact: A release cannot be independently reconstructed from one signed machine-verifiable manifest.
risks.acceptance: Every release publishes one sanitized manifest containing frontend SHA, Worker SHA/version, API/schema/methodology versions, migration state, audit run, and rollback reference.

risks.summary: No application workflow exists for user export, account deletion, retention, periodic backup, restore drill, or immutable audit export.
risks.impact: Data loss recovery and user data rights cannot be reliably executed or evidenced.
risks.acceptance: Export, deletion, retention, encrypted backup, restore drill, RPO, RTO, and audit procedures are implemented and tested.

risks.summary: Transactions store only a date; production calculation falls back to a fixed BUY then DIV then SELL order for same-day records.
risks.impact: FIFO, realized P&L, oversell detection, day trades, and dividend entitlement can be wrong for same-day activity.
risks.acceptance: New fills preserve executed UTC time and broker sequence; legacy date-only rows remain explicitly marked rather than assigned fabricated times.

risks.summary: Scheduled all-user calculation builds a shared ticker universe and performs shared market and calendar preparation before tenant-level failure isolation.
risks.impact: One tenant's invalid or unsupported instrument can block updates for every tenant and amplify shared market-data load.
risks.acceptance: Scheduler creates independent tenant jobs and one tenant failure cannot prevent unrelated tenant publication.

risks.summary: Signed cursor pagination is deterministic but is not bound to a ledger revision or database snapshot.
risks.impact: Concurrent creates, updates, or deletes between pages can cause undetectable missing records even when duplicate-page checks pass.
risks.acceptance: All pages bind to one ledger revision and a mid-read mutation returns a deterministic restart response.

risks.summary: Snapshot insert and retention deletion are separate operations without an atomic latest pointer.
risks.impact: An upload can be visible even when the API reports failure, duplicate on retry, or leave retention cleanup incomplete.
risks.acceptance: Staged snapshots publish through an atomic pointer only after validation; cleanup is asynchronous and idempotent.

risks.summary: Dispatch timeout, callback loss, rerun metadata, and unexpected exceptions can leave queued or running jobs orphaned or misclassified.
risks.impact: Users can see permanent in-progress state while data is updated, or retry into duplicate work.
risks.acceptance: Lease, heartbeat, dispatch identity, rerun attempt, sweeper, expiry, supersede, and result-snapshot linkage resolve every terminal path.

risks.summary: Each browser tab and device independently triggers three-minute market-hours updates, and the pause control does not stop the refresh timer.
risks.impact: One user can create repeated jobs, queue pressure, and unnecessary market-data downloads while UI claims refresh is paused.
risks.acceptance: Cross-tab leader election, visibility handling, actual pause enforcement, and server-side coalescing produce one active refresh per tenant input revision.

risks.summary: Token refresh initialization occurs before restored login state and does not watch later token changes; JWT decoding is duplicated and one path lacks padding.
risks.impact: Periodic refresh can remain disabled and users are logged out only after an API request fails.
risks.acceptance: One tested auth service watches token/session state and boundary-time tests prove refresh and logout behavior across tabs.

risks.summary: Benchmark setting changes immediately while the visible snapshot does not identify which benchmark produced its stored benchmark return series.
risks.impact: A chart can be labeled with a newly requested benchmark while still displaying an older benchmark's data.
risks.acceptance: Snapshot carries benchmark identity and UI distinguishes current published benchmark from a pending requested benchmark.

risks.summary: API accepts economically invalid or unsupported records such as future dates and zero-price buys or sells that later fail or corrupt calculation semantics.
risks.impact: A record accepted as successful can make every later calculation fail closed.
risks.acceptance: Type-specific validation and supported-instrument rules warn under legacy contract, then fail closed under a versioned contract after client migration.

risks.summary: One API secret authorizes all-user records reads, snapshot writes, job callbacks, and also signs cursors.
risks.impact: Compromise of any runner or callback credential grants a broad cross-tenant blast radius and forces coupled rotation.
risks.acceptance: Service credentials have independent scope, audience, expiry, key ID, rotation overlap, and replay protection.

risks.summary: Symbol syntax permits indices, FX, futures-like, crypto-like, and foreign instruments that the equity accounting model does not support.
risks.impact: Unsupported asset classes can be silently valued and taxed as ordinary USD equities.
risks.acceptance: An instrument master classifies exchange, currency, asset class, multiplier, and support status; unsupported classes cannot publish verified results.

risks.summary: Fees and taxes are forced non-negative and normalized with abs, so rebates, refunds, ADR fees, and cash adjustments cannot be represented faithfully.
risks.impact: Broker corrections and tax refunds must be hidden in notes or distort trade economics.
risks.acceptance: Explicit typed cash events represent charges and reversals without overloading transaction fee fields.

risks.summary: Snapshot updated_at has minute precision and no timezone or monotonic revision.
risks.impact: Two updates in one minute can be indistinguishable and displayed time is ambiguous between UTC and local time.
risks.acceptance: RFC3339 UTC timestamp, immutable snapshot ID, and monotonic revision replace display time as update identity.

risks.summary: All-user runs publish each successful tenant immediately but report the whole workflow failed when a later tenant fails, without an explicit batch model.
risks.impact: Operations cannot distinguish total failure from partial tenant success or reliably retry only failed members.
risks.acceptance: Calculation batches track total, succeeded, failed, skipped, and superseded tenant members while publication remains tenant-atomic.

risks.summary: General authenticated fetches lack timeout, cancellation, latest-request-wins control, and mutation-aware retry policy.
risks.impact: A half-open request can leave loading or trigger state pending indefinitely and a late response can overwrite newer state.
risks.acceptance: Reads use bounded timeout and cancellation; mutations retry only with idempotency identity; stale responses cannot overwrite newer state.

risks.summary: Health only checks core table existence and schema version.
risks.impact: The service can report healthy while indexes, recent calculations, market freshness, snapshot integrity, or job backlog are unhealthy.
risks.acceptance: Liveness, readiness, dependency, and protected data-quality checks are separated and alert on stale snapshots and orphan jobs without exposing tenant data.

risks.summary: Pages CSP permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval while tokens and transaction data are stored in localStorage.
risks.impact: A script injection has a high-impact path to credentials and financial data.
risks.acceptance: CSP is tightened in staging with Google sign-in compatibility, unsafe-eval is removed, and sensitive browser persistence is eliminated before production cutover.
